To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

different tests of reading measure different aspects of reading, that different reading tests are more or less dependent on different aspects of language and that different tests of comprehension are more or less heavily dependent on different aspects and different levels of language comprehension.
different measures of reading ability tap different underlying skills and that the most appropriate test for a particular child will depend on the nature of the child's difficulties.

1) different reading tests measure distinct aspects of the reading system and 2) tests of reading comprehension that are heavily dependent on language comprehension are more difficult for children with poor comprehension than those that are more heavily dependent on decoding skill.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature of the relationship between tests of reading accuracy and reading comprehension.
the nature of reading difficulties in children and the assessment of these difficulties.
the validity of current measures of children’s reading skills and the extent to which they tap the same underlying processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the assessment of reading ability is not a simple matter and the use of a range of different measures of reading ability is to be recommended.
there are no tests of reading comprehension, and no tests of reading accuracy.
the assessment of reading ability is a complex process and that a range of different tests are required in order to provide a full picture of an individual's strengths and weaknesses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
reading comprehension is not simply a matter of reading accuracy but that it is also heavily dependent on linguistic and cognitive skills.

tests of word reading and tests of comprehension measure different aspects of reading skill and that the relative contributions of different reading skills to overall reading comprehension will vary according to the nature of the reading task and the age of the child.
reading tests should not be used as interchangeable measures of reading skill, but rather that they are best viewed as tapping different aspects of the underlying reading process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
different reading measures assess different aspects of the underlying cognitive skills.
different reading tests do not all tap the same underlying skill and that the nature of the reading difficulties that a child has can be inferred from the pattern of their reading test performance.
different tests of reading measure different aspects of reading and should not be used interchangeably.
